title: SDK Galaxy handoff mini-playbook (draft)
abstract: A compact, minute-driven playbook for quickly handing off a minimal SDK integration to a partner team. Emphasizes CLI-first paths, short labs, lightweight telemetry opt-in, and a single-file sampleapp to ship in 15 minutes.
body:
Purpose and audience:
- Audience: PMs + single engineer (or contractor) who need to validate an SDK integration end-to-end in one pairing session.
- Purpose: give a reproducible 15-minute flow that produces a deployed sample and clears common friction points.

High-level constraints (why this doc exists):
- Keep friction < 15 minutes total.
- Avoid language or infra assumptions: CLI + Docker + simple static site are the only pre-reqs.
- Provide clear rollback / remove commands.

Setup assumptions (pre-work, 3–5 mins if done ahead):
- Sign up for Redwood sandbox account (free credits) and create API key.
- Install redwood-cli (npm i -g @redwood/infer-cli) OR use the provided docker wrapper.
- Have git and Docker available locally.

15-minute script (minute-by-minute):
0:00–1:30 — Welcome and goal (one sentence): ship a minimal sampleapp that calls the hosted API and renders a streaming response. Confirm roles.
1:30–3:00 — Verify environment: run `redwood --version` and `docker --version`. If CLI missing: run `npx @redwood/infer-cli@latest --help` as fallback.
3:00–6:00 — Fetch sample repo and set API key:
  - git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-samples.git 
  - cd sdk-samples/minisite-stub
  - copy API key to `.env.local` (example provided in repo).
6:00–9:00 — Run sample in local Docker to simulate production request patterns:
  - docker-compose up --build (or `npm run dev` if preferring Node).
  - Open http://localhost:3000 and trigger a sample prompt.
9:00–11:00 — Observe telemetry & basic metrics:
  - Use built-in /telemetry endpoint in sample to show request latency, token count, and error rates.
  - Demonstrate how trace id surfaces in Redwood Console (quick link).
11:00–13:30 — Make a small change and re-run (confidence check):
  - tweak prompt template in src/prompts.js (append a clarifying instruction).
  - save, restart, re-run flow, observe result diff.
13:30–15:00 — Commit, open PR template, and closeout:
  - git checkout -b tiny-onramp && git add . && git commit -m "mini: add sample prompt tweak" && git push origin tiny-onramp
  - Show PR checklist (telemetry enabled, token budget noted, stake-holder tagged).

Quick troubleshooting cheats (one-liners):
- API auth error: run `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=xxx` (or put in .env.local).
- Rate limited: `redwood requests inspect --last 10` to see quota headers and sample ids.
- Streaming not working in browser: ensure `EventSource` polyfill is loaded, or test with `redwood stream --prompt "test"` from CLI.

Handoff checklist (what to leave with the receiving team):
- Link to the running sandbox demo (public or ephemeral).
- A short PR with the sample change + the PR checklist.
- A single-line README addition: how to rotate API keys and where telemetry is stored.
- One prompt test case (in `tests/acceptance/quickstart.prompts.txt`).

Privacy and telemetry opt-in model (keeps legal happy):
- Default sample toggles telemetry OFF. For pairing sessions we enable opt-in sampling via `.env.local` flag: `REDWOOD_SAMPLE_TELEMETRY=true`.
- Collected fields: request id, model, token counts, latency, error code. No raw user PII or prompt storage unless explicitly opted in and signed DPA approved.

Template PR checklist (paste into PR body):
- [ ] Telemetry toggled appropriately for staging
- [ ] Sample prompt included and labelled as non-prod
- [ ] Token budget commented in PR description
- [ ] Reviewer: eng-developer-experience
- [ ] Optional: include screenshot of console latency for at least one request

Open questions / TODOs (work-in-progress):
- Can we ship a tiny cross-platform binary for the CLI fallback to avoid npm/Docker friction? (Miguel to prototype).
- Should the sample default to a cheap quantized model? Tradeoff: lower cost vs reproducibility across accounts.
- Add a 5-minute smoke test checklist for security reviewers to validate before demos to customers.

Notes to self / pair-session oopsies I've seen:
- People copy the sample env into production; we should strongly label the README with explicit non-prod warnings.
- Telemetry paths are surprising to PMs — add a little GIF in the README showing where latency and tokens show up.
- Network proxies in some corp laptops block streaming; advise using the CLI wrapper which falls back to polling.

Appendix: small set of commands to include in a one-file quickstart (drop into README):
- `git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-samples.git && cd sdk-samples/minisite-stub`
- `cp .env.example .env.local && edit .env.local`
- `docker compose up --build` OR `npm run dev`
- Trigger: open browser to / and click "Ask"
- Remove demo: `docker compose down --volumes` and `git branch -D tiny-onramp`

If this flows well in two pair-sessions, convert to an explainer-deck (5 slides) + one-minute demo video and add to the onboarding portal.
